column2: {Check your components to make sure they're all there.;Sometimes a small part is hidden in the bag. Take a close look here.;The colors or the number of bands on the resistors may vary. We use components from various manufacturers.;Tip: These are exclusively THT (through-hole) components. Insert the components through the circuit board from the top and solder them in place from the other side. You can gently bend the legs on the back as you insert them{
column3: }so the parts stay in place and are easier to solder.}

column2: {Flip the circuit board over to the back (the text “Smartphone Robot” is printed on the front).;Insert the two LDRs into the light\_sensor1 and light\_sensor2 sockets and solder them in place. The LDR sensors are not polarized.; Trim the excess wires.}

{Flip the circuit board back to the front.;Solder the resistors resistor1 + resistor2 \usePart{resistor12} and resistor\_led1 \usePart{resistorled1} in place. The color code shows you the resistance values. Alternatively
column3: you can measure the resistance values with a multimeter.;Trim the excess wire on the back.;Caution: When cutting
column4: the leads tend to fly around and can pop into your eyes. Wear safety goggles!}

column2: {Now solder the led1 in place.;Caution: LEDs are directional. The long leg is the ‘+’ side. A hole on the circuit board is also marked with a plus sign. Insert the long leg through the hole on the circuit board marked with a +.;After soldering
column3: trim the excess wires on the back.}

column2: {Now insert the push\_button switch. To do this
column3: bend the solder tabs down 90°.;Then solder the tabs securely on the other side.;Trim the excess wire.}

column2: {Insert the transistors into the circuit board from the front. The black part must face the “Smartphone Robot” label. Solder each of the three legs in place.; Cut off the excess wires.}
{If you have motors without wires: Solder the wires to the motors. One color on the left and one on the right. This way
column4: both motors will have the same color on the left and the same color on the right.; Secure the wires with a cable tie.}

column2: {Gather the round wooden discs.;Take a d=70 disc with a small hole.;Glue the D=68mm disc onto it
column3: centered.;Then glue a d=70mm disc with an oval hole onto the d=68mm disc
column4: centered. ;Once everything is dry and secure: Thread a rubber band onto the rim.;Repeat this for the second rim.}

column2: {Now glue the remaining wooden pieces together. Make sure the small compartment is at the front near the holes and the large compartment is at the back with the label.; Place the square wooden board centered on the bottom so that half of it extends toward the circular holes.;Tip: You can secure the wooden pieces with masking tape until the wood glue dries.}
{Now cut off the plug at the end of the battery holder cable.; Strip about 5 mm of insulation from the wires.;Then tin the ends with solder.;Next
column3: solder the black wire to the negative (-) terminal and the red wire to the positive (+) terminal.}

column2: {Now solder on the motors.; Caution: Look closely at the picture. If the wires on the motors are facing toward you (yellow part at the bottom)
column3: the left wire must go into the hole on the circuit board that is closer to the “Smartphone Robot” label.;The right wire then goes into the other hole.}

column2: {Now attach the tires to the motors.; The motor wires must point to the left later (see photo).; Push the tires firmly onto the axle.; Glue the circuit board to the front at the marked spot.; You can insert the battery compartment into the rear compartment right away.; Tip: In the photo
column3: you can already see where the motors should be glued. But be sure to check out the next step before gluing them in place.}

column2: {Now glue the motors in place. The tires should be low enough that the square plate stands upright on the table.;Use some hot glue to secure them.;Glue the motors to the back sides of the wooden box (see photo from the previous step).}
{Now glue a bottle cap (either metal or plastic) onto the square wooden plate.;This will cause the robot to tilt back slightly.}
